source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-17

procedures.title: Refrigerant-12: handling precautions
steps: Do not heat the container on a gas stove or radiator or with a blow torch; use only a bucket of warm water (125°F maximum) or warm wet rags.
Do not rely on the safety plug; drums have burst when it failed.
Do not weld or steam clean on or near the system; pressure can build to a dangerous level.
When filling a small drum from a large one, never fill it completely; leave space above the liquid for expansion.
Avoid breathing large amounts of R-12 after an accidental rapid discharge, especially where a flame device such as a gas heater is present.
Wear goggles or glasses when working around the system.

If liquid R-12 gets in the eyes: stay calm and do not rub them; flood the area with lots of cold water to bring it gradually above freezing; apply mineral, cod liver or antiseptic oil as a protective film against infection; see an eye specialist as soon as possible.
notes: Strong concentrations of R-12 meeting a live flame produce a toxic gas that also attacks bright metal.
Any liquid R-12 that touches you is at least 21.7°F below zero.
Releasing large amounts of R-12 into a room is normally harmless.

procedures.title: Refrigerant lines: handling precautions
steps: Keep metal tubing free of kinks; one kink can greatly reduce system capacity.
Never bend a flexible hose to a radius under 10 times its diameter.
Keep flexible hoses at least 2-1/2" away from the exhaust manifold.
Inspect flexible hoses at least yearly for leaks or brittleness and replace any that fail.
Use only sealed lines from parts stock.
Discharge all refrigerant before opening any fitting; even so, open it very slowly with face and hands clear, and bleed off any pressure slowly.
Wear safety goggles whenever opening a refrigerant line.
Cap any line opened to atmosphere at once to keep out moisture and dirt.
Use the correct wrenches on O-ring fittings and back up the opposing fitting with a wrench.
On flexible hose connections, hold the swaged fitting, the flare nut and the coupling with three separate wrenches so the fitting does not turn and damage the seat.
Make sure O-rings and seats are perfect; a burr or speck of dirt can leak.
Make sure sealing beads on hose clamp connections are free of nicks and scratches.

procedures.title: Refrigeration system: maintaining chemical stability
notes: Internal metal parts, refrigerant and oil stay chemically stable only with pure R-12 and clean refrigeration oil.

Dirt, air or moisture upset this; heat speeds them into acids and sludge that break down components, and they also distort the R-12 temperature-pressure relationship, lowering efficiency (see figure 23 in the manual).
